question: to the Commission Eleonora Meleti (PPE) Subject:

In recent years, several Member States have seen an increase in cases of abuse against older persons either in the form of physical, psychological or verbal violence or neglect by caregivers. This is a serious social problem the European Union is facing and one that is underreported and not highlighted enough. The demographic evolution in the European Union and the ever-increasing need for long-term care services make it necessary to enhance the quality of the services provided through the development of prevention, inspection and reporting systems, as well as to further strengthen the professionalism of the sector, provide ongoing training for carers and ensure safe and decent care conditions for older persons. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What measures does it intend to take and how does it plan to support Member States in preventing and addressing the mistreatment of older persons in situations of dependency?

Is it considering establishing common European standards for the training, certification, supervision and assessment of carers looking after older people, to ensure the quality and safety of care provided?

Does it intend to promote the collection of comparable data from across the EU concerning cases of abuse of older persons and the quality of long-term care services, as part of the European Care Strategy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.6.2026) The Commission supports Member States to prevent and address the mistreatment of older persons, in line with the European Care Strategy1 and the Council Recommendation on LongTerm Care2 (LTC). This encompasses technical support and EU funds, such as Cohesion funds or the Recovery and Resilience Facility, and mutual learning. In addition, the Commission, in cooperation with the World Health Organisation, supports Member States improve the quality of LTC services across all care settings through mutual learning and compiles data on LTC quality management. The Recommendation on LTC underscores the need for adequate training and working conditions for care professionals. To support this, the Commission has launched the LargeScale Skills Partnership for LTC to equip workers with digital and person-centred care skills. The European Social Fund plus helps reskill and upskill care workers and funds measures to help improve their working conditions. To underpin monitoring efforts, the Commission and the Social Protection Committee developed a Monitoring Framework, which establishes a core set of LTC indicators, including policy levers on LTC quality. The Commission will report to the Council on the implementation of the Recommendation on LTC and put forward a European Care Deal in 2027. In 2023, the Commission proposed a Regulation on the protection of adults in cross-border situations. The Regulation aims to safeguard adults who, due to a disability or health-related limitations, are not in a position to fully protect their own interests in cross-border situations and to ensure that their right to individual autonomy is maintained when they move or reside across Member States3.
